synthesis.project_summary: The Example Lighthouse Service ran a nationally coordinated network of 47 coastal stations for nearly a century, with keepers held to strict operational routines that shaped both daily life and station design.
synthesis.research_question: How did the Example Lighthouse Service standardize operations across 47 coastal stations?
open_questions: The exact rationale for the 1925 electrification timeline is not detailed in the collected sources.
research_gaps: No source in this batch covers keeper training procedures directly.
suggested_script_angles: Frame around a single keeper's daily routine as a lens into the whole system.
prohibited_unsafe_assertions: Do not claim all 47 stations electrified simultaneously — the sources do not support a single uniform date.

sources.title: Example Lighthouse Service Historical Overview
sources.relevant_excerpt: The Example Lighthouse Service operated 47 stations along the eastern coast between 1852 and 1939, transitioning from oil lamps to electric beacons by 1925.

sources.title: Daily Life of a 19th-Century Lighthouse Keeper
sources.relevant_excerpt: Keepers were required to log weather conditions every four hours and maintain a two-year supply of oil on isolated stations, a requirement that shaped station architecture.

verified_fact.claim_text: The Example Lighthouse Service operated 47 stations along the eastern coast between 1852 and 1939.
